## Captain's intent
Hackathon {Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack Zuerich, 2026-10-10, Live-Demo 20:00. Produkt "Micro Intent" (Look and say). Das Team hat sich auf eine iPhone-App festgelegt (SwiftUI, a2ui-swift, Gradium-Stimme, WebSocket-Backend von Igor).
Captain-Wort: "ganz wichtig jetzt dass wir an der mobilen app arbeiten", "wir machen erstmal nur die UI", und Entire muss nach den Richtlinien genutzt werden.

Projekt: https://github.com/Orb-agent/micro-intent (umgezogen von BatuCani/micro-intent; die alte URL leitet weiter).
Massgeblich ist der Team-Plan auf Branch develop: docs/work-packages.md, Abschnitt "WP1: Frontend, iPhone app", und docs/contracts.md (WebSocket, Audio, Cards, A2UI). Zuerst beide lesen; der Vertrag ist die API zwischen den Devs und wird nicht umgangen.

Auftrag: WP1 nur UI, Tasks 1-5 und 8 aus WP1, gegen Fixtures:
1. Xcode-Projekt frontend/BeaverAgent (SwiftUI, iOS 17, NSMicrophoneUsageDescription), a2ui-swift from 0.3.0, Produkt A2UISwiftUI. Keine weiteren Pakete.
2. Fixtures aus contracts.md (A2UI-Beispiel), dazu backend/fixtures/cards.json und demo_reply.json aus Igors Branch feature/wp2-backend-voice-vision.
3. Kartenansicht: a2ui.messages decodieren, A2UISurfaceView; alle vier Kartentypen aus den Fixtures, hell und dunkel. Wenn a2ui-swift mehr als 30 min Probleme macht: native SwiftUI-Karten aus reply.cards.
4. Orb mit Zustaenden idle/listening/thinking/searching/speaking und Label, Maskottchen-Blase mit reply.say.
5. Einstellungen (Server-URL, Token per @AppStorage) und WebSocket-Client per Vertrag, Long-Press auf den Orb oeffnet ein Debug-Textfeld. Gegen Igors Stub nur, wenn erreichbar; sonst ist der Fixture-Modus der Default.
8. Screen-Chip bei screen_ok.
Nicht im Umfang: Mikrofon, Wiedergabe, Hands-free (WP1 Tasks 6-7), Backend-Aenderungen.

Look: dunkles Glas wie im Paper-Prototyp Variante D (dunkle transluzente Flaechen, feiner heller Rand, weicher Schatten, Orb als Fokus, grosse gut lesbare Schrift fuer aeltere Nutzer, Bestaetigen/Abbrechen als grosse Buttons). Nichts aus fremden Marken kopieren.

Entire nach Richtlinien: Das Repo hat .entire/settings.json (enabled, Checkpoints in git-refs). Entire-CLI liegt unter /opt/homebrew/bin/entire. Vor dem Arbeiten im Worktree pruefen, dass `entire status` aktiv ist (sonst `entire enable --agent claude-code`), Checkpoint-Refs mit pushen, AGENTS.md des Repos inklusive .entire/graph-agent.md befolgen.

   Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor
   would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the
   needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines;
   firstmate reads your pane for that.
   Whenever you mention a PR anywhere - a status line, your terminal, a summary - write its full
   https:// URL exactly as the forge printed it, never a bare number such as "PR 108"; firstmate
   copies that URL from your line rather than assembling one.
   A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the
   turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done.
   Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a
   known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window, or your own validation round):
   firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long
   cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help.
5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked [at=<epoch>]: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help.

# Contracts (MVP)

The interfaces between the three [work packages](work-packages.md). If something here doesn't fit, raise it with the team before coding around it.

## Stack

| Part | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend (iPhone) | SwiftUI, iOS 17+, `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, `AVAudioEngine`, [a2ui-swift](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift) `from: "0.3.0"` (product `A2UISwiftUI`) |
| Backend | Python 3.11, uv, FastAPI and uvicorn, httpx, `google-genai`, `gradium`, python-dotenv, pytest |
| Hosting | Server on a dev Mac; a Cloudflare quick tunnel gives the HTTPS and WSS URL that the app and the Shortcut use. Start it once and leave it running: the URL changes on every restart |
| Time zone | `Europe/Zurich` everywhere; times on the wire are ISO 8601 with offset |

```text
frontend/               # WP1: Xcode project, SwiftUI
backend/                # run from here: uv run uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000
  pyproject.toml        # WP2 owns it; lists every package's deps
  .env.example
  app.py  voice.py  vision.py      # WP2
  a2ui.py                          # WP3: cards → A2UI messages
  agent.py  context.py  tools/sbb.py   # WP3
  fixtures/             # demo_reply.json, cards.json, screen.json, screen.png (WP2); context.json, *_a2ui.json (WP3)
  tests/
```

## One turn

The screenshot arrives before the question, so vision runs while the user is still talking.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant SC as Shortcut
  participant App as App (WP1)
  participant S as Server (WP2)
  participant V as Vision (WP2)
  participant G as Gradium
  participant A as Agent (WP3)
  SC->>S: POST /screenshot
  S->>V: read_screen(image), in the background
  V-->>S: ScreenContext
  S->>App: screen_ok {summary}
  App->>S: audio × n, then audio_end
  S->>G: stream mic audio, flush
  G-->>S: transcript segments
  S->>App: state thinking, transcript
  S->>A: turn(text, screen, on_status)
  A-->>S: on_status("Checking trains…")
  S->>App: state searching + label
  A-->>S: Reply {say, cards}
  S->>App: reply, a2ui, state speaking
  S->>G: TTS say
  G-->>S: audio chunks
  S->>App: audio × n, audio_end, state idle
```

## WebSocket `/ws`

JSON text frames only, one object per frame, discriminated by `type`. Audio is base64 inside JSON. The app sends `hello` first; the server closes the socket on a wrong token.

**App → server**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hello` | `token` | First frame after connecting |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM, see [Audio](#audio) | Every 80 ms while the orb is held |
| `audio_end` | — | Orb released; the server finalizes STT and runs the turn |
| `text` | `text` | Typed question (debug field); runs a turn without STT |
| `screen` | `mime`, `data`: base64 | Optional: an image picked in the app, for rehearsals. Same effect as `POST /screenshot` |

**Server → app**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | — | After a valid `hello` |
| `state` | `state`: `idle` \| `listening` \| `thinking` \| `searching` \| `speaking`; `label`?: string | On every change; `label` is the tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…" |
| `transcript` | `text` | Final transcript of the user's turn |
| `reply` | `say`, `cards`: see [Cards](#cards) | Before any of the turn's audio |
| `a2ui` | `messages`: list of A2UI v0.9 messages, see [A2UI](#a2ui) | Right after `reply`, when it has cards |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM | TTS chunks for the last `reply` |
| `audio_end` | — | TTS for the last `reply` is complete |
| `screen_ok` | `summary`?: string | Vision has read a new screenshot; `summary` is missing if vision failed |
| `error` | `message` | Turn failed; the server then sends `state: idle` |

The orb shows `speaking` while the app still has audio queued, even after the server has sent `state: idle`.

## HTTP

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /screenshot` | From the iPhone Shortcut. `Authorization: Bearer <APP_TOKEN>`, body is the raw image (`image/jpeg` or `image/png`, max 8 MB). Returns `204` and starts vision |
| `GET /health` | `{"ok": true, "workspace": "rest" \| "fixture"}` |

**Screenshot rule:** the server keeps only the latest screenshot and its `ScreenContext`. A turn gets the context if the screenshot is less than 120 s old and no earlier turn has used it; if vision is still running, the turn waits for it.

## Audio

Both directions use Gradium's native format, so the server forwards the base64 strings without decoding them.

| Direction | Format | Gradium side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mic, app → server | PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz; 80 ms chunks = 1920 samples = 3840 bytes | STT setup `input_format: "pcm"` |
| TTS, server → app | Same format, chunks as Gradium sends them | TTS setup `output_format: "pcm_24000"` (the default `pcm` is 48 kHz) |

**iPhone side:** audio session `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, or iOS plays through the quiet earpiece while the mic is on. Turn on echo cancellation with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` before reading the input format. Convert the input with `AVAudioConverter` to Int16 at 24 kHz mono. Play through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine, converting each chunk to a Float32 24 kHz buffer.

**Gradium facts the server relies on** ([docs](https://docs.gradium.ai/api-reference/introduction)): auth header `x-api-key`; STT at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`, TTS at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts`; the Python SDK is `pip install gradium`. STT needs `json_config.language` (`en` for the demo, `any` to auto-detect). STT sends `text` segments, not partial and final flags. On push-to-talk release the server sends `flush`, waits for `flushed`, and joins the segments into the transcript. TTS has no cancel message: closing the socket stops it. The free plan allows 2 TTS and 3 STT sessions at once, which is tight with 3 devs testing; the $13 XS plan raises that to 5 and 20.

`reply.cards` holds 0 to 3 cards. The model fills them from tool results and context, and the server passes them through after validation. Optional fields may be missing. The app renders the `a2ui` messages built from these cards; native SwiftUI cards from `reply.cards` are the fallback.

| `kind` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `train` | `line` ("IC 8"), `from`, `to`, `departure`, `arrival`, `platform`?, `transfers`, `delay_min`? |
| `conflict` | `event` {`title`, `start`, `end`}, `proposal` {`title`, `start`, `place`?}, `verdict`: `fits` \| `tight` \| `clash`, `note`? |
| `event` | `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`?, `source`: `calendar` \| `luma` |
| `flight` | `flight_number`, `from`, `to` (IATA or city), `departure`, `arrival`, `booking_ref`? |

```json

    {"id": "c1-body", "component": "Column", "children": ["c1-time", "c1-line", "c1-meta"]},

```


## Agent interface

What WP2's server calls and WP3 implements in `agent.py`. WP2's `StubAgent` has the same shape and returns `demo_reply.json`.

```python
from typing import Awaitable, Callable, TypedDict

class Reply(TypedDict):
    say: str          # one or two short sentences, the user's language
    cards: list[dict] # see Cards

class Agent:
    async def start(self) -> None:
        """Once per WebSocket session: load_context() and build the system prompt."""

    async def turn(
        self,
        text: str,
        screen: dict | None,  # ScreenContext, see Screen context
        on_status: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],  # tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…"
    ) -> Reply:
        """One user turn. Keeps conversation history on self. Never raises for model
        or tool errors: returns a short apology with no cards instead."""
```

## Tools

**Model-facing.** The model sees two functions and must end every turn with `respond`.

| Function | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sbb_connections` | `from_station`, `to_station`, `depart_after` (ISO) | `{"connections": [{"line", "from", "to", "departure", "arrival", "platform", "arrival_platform", "transfers", "delay_min", "duration_min"}]}`, at most 4 |
| `respond` | `say`, `cards` (see [Cards](#cards)) | Ends the turn |

`sbb_connections` calls `GET https://transport.opendata.ch/v1/connections?from=…&to=…&date=YYYY-MM-DD&time=HH:MM&limit=4` (no key). Map `products[0]` → `line`, `from.platform` → `platform`, `to.platform` → `arrival_platform`, `from.delay` → `delay_min`.

**Gemini rules** (`google-genai`, `generate_content`, checked 2026-10-10; they apply to vision too):

- Model `gemini-3.8-flash` with thinking level `low`. `gemini-3.5-flash` was deprecated on 8 October 2026. Don't set temperature; Gemini 3.6 and later ignore it.
- Declare functions with `parameters_json_schema`. For `cards.items`, use `anyOf` with one object per kind, each with a single-value `enum` on `kind`. Don't use `const`, `oneOf` or `$defs`, keep it shallow, and validate the arguments in code anyway.
- Function calling mode `ANY` on every step, so the model always calls `sbb_connections` or `respond` and never returns free text. On the last step add `allowed_function_names=["respond"]`.
- Append `response.candidates[0].content` to the history unmodified; it carries the thought signatures, and dropping them gives a 400. Then add one function response per call, with the call's `id` and `name`, after all the calls.
- Vision attaches the screenshot as an inline image part at medium media resolution (560 tokens); use high if small chat text comes back wrong.

**Context.** `context.load_context()` runs once per session and goes into the system prompt as JSON:

```json

  "events": [{"title": "Call with Acme", "start": "2026-10-15T17:30:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-15T17:45:00+02:00", "location": "Zoom", "source": "calendar"}],
  "flight_emails": [{"subject": "Your booking K7Q2ZP: Zürich – Lisbon", "from": "SWISS", "date": "2026-10-09", "body": "first 2000 characters of the text body"}]
}
```

Events cover now to 7 days ahead. `source` is `luma` when the event's description or organizer mentions lu.ma. `WORKSPACE_MODE=fixture` returns `fixtures/context.json` with this exact shape.

**Workspace access:** REST with a refresh token for the temporary account. Switch to them only if we're already enrolled.

Each of these fits without breaking the contract above:

- **Filler line:** an extra short `reply` with no cards, spoken while a tool runs.
- **Barge-in:** an `interrupt` message from the app; the server cancels the turn and closes the TTS socket.
- **Card actions** (move, skip, keep): A2UI `Button` actions sent back as an `action` message.

# A2UI-Swift **Render AI-generated JSON as safe native Apple UI.** ![a2ui](./a2ui.png) [![Swift](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-5.9+-F05138?logo=swift&logoColor=white)](https://swift.org) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platforms-iOS%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20tvOS%20%7C%20watchOS%20%7C%20visionOS-007AFF?logo=apple)](#requirements) [![SPM](https://img.shields.io/badge/SwiftPM-compatible-brightgreen)](#installation) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/DocC-documentation-blue?logo=swift&logoColor=white)](https://bbc6bae9.github.io/a2ui-swift/documentation/) [![A2UI Spec](https://img.shields.io/badge/A2UI%20spec-v0.9.1-8A2BE2)](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift?style=social)](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift/stargazers)
AI agents are getting good at deciding what interface a user needs next: a form, an approval card, a search result list, a booking panel, or a small workflow UI. But shipping executable UI code from an agent into an iOS or macOS app is not a serious production boundary. Web views are easy to embed, but they often lose native behavior, accessibility, styling, and platform trust. **A2UI-Swift** takes a different path: ```text Agent -> declarative A2UI JSON -> A2UI-Swift -> SwiftUI / UIKit / AppKit ``` The agent describes **what** should be rendered. Your app keeps control of **how** it is rendered, which components are allowed, how actions are handled, and what data can flow back. [A2UI](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) is an open protocol from Google for agent-to-user interfaces. **A2UI-Swift** is a community-maintained Apple-platform renderer, listed in the [official A2UI renderer ecosystem](https://a2ui.org/ecosystem/renderers/). ## Why This Exists Modern AI apps need richer output than Markdown, but most options come with tradeoffs: | Approach | Problem | | --- | --- | | Ask the model to generate SwiftUI code | Unsafe to execute and hard to review at runtime | | Embed remote HTML in a web view | Easy to ship, but not truly native | | Build one-off dynamic screens | Expensive to maintain across products | | Hard-code every agent response | Safe, but too rigid for adaptive workflows | A2UI-Swift is built for the middle ground: **agent-generated UI as data, rendered through trusted native controls**. ## What You Get - **Native rendering across Apple platforms**: SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit renderers share one protocol model. - **A2UI v0.9 / v0.9.1 support**: message processing, surfaces, data model updates, actions, expressions, checks, templates, and catalogs. - **17 built-in components**: Text, Image, Icon, Button, TextField, CheckBox, Slider, ChoicePicker, DateTimeInput, Row, Column, List, Card, Tabs, Modal, Divider, AudioPlayer, and Video. - **Two-way data binding**: inputs write back to the local data model, while streaming agent updates can rebuild or update the UI in place. - **Custom component catalogs**: expose your own trusted SwiftUI, UIKit, or AppKit components to the agent without allowing arbitrary code execution. - **Localization support**: Foundation number, currency, date formatting, and pluralization using the system ICU/CLDR rules. Pluralization requires the bundled `PluralCategories.stringsdict`; rule versions and numeric boundaries follow the OS and may differ from JavaScript `Intl.PluralRules`. - **Test coverage**: 300+ tests across protocol decoding, expression evaluation, data binding, validation, and renderer behavior. ## Quick Start ### SwiftUI ```swift import A2UISwiftUI @State var viewModel = SurfaceViewModel(catalog: basicCatalog) try viewModel.processMessages(messages) A2UISurfaceView(viewModel: viewModel) { action in print("Action:", action.name) } ``` ### UIKit ```swift import A2UISwiftCore import A2UIUIKit let hostView = A2UISurfaceHostView() let processor = MessageProcessor(catalogs: [catalog]) { action in print("Action:", action.name) } processor.processMessages(messages) if let surface = processor.model.getSurface(surfaceId) { hostView.render(surface: surface, rootComponentId: "root") } ``` ### AppKit ```swift import A2UISwiftCore import A2UIAppKit let hostView = A2UISurfaceHostView() let processor = MessageProcessor(catalogs: [catalog]) { action in print("Action:", action.name) } processor.processMessages(messages) if let surface = processor.model.getSurface(surfaceId) { hostView.render(surface: surface, rootComponentId: "root") } ``` ## Installation Add A2UI-Swift through Swift Package Manager: ```swift dependencies: [ .package(url: "https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift", from: "0.3.0"), ] ``` Then import the renderer you need: ```swift import A2UISwiftUI import A2UIUIKit import A2UIAppKit ``` ## Requirements | Platform | Minimum version | | --- | --- | | iOS / tvOS | 17.0 | | macOS | 14.0 | | watchOS | 10.0 | | visionOS | 1.0 | ## Modules The package is split into focused library products, so apps can depend only on the pieces they need. | Module | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `A2UISwiftCore` | Shared protocol layer: schema, data model, catalogs, expressions, actions, and message processing | | `A2UISwiftUI` | SwiftUI renderer through `A2UISurfaceView` and `SurfaceViewModel` | | `A2UIUIKit` | UIKit renderer for iOS, tvOS, and visionOS through `A2UISurfaceHostView` | | `A2UIAppKit` | AppKit renderer for macOS through `A2UISurfaceHostView` | | `Primitives` | Shared primitive types such as `ChatMessage`, `Part`, `JSONValue`, and `ToolDefinition` | | `v_08` | Deprecated v0.8 renderer kept for legacy sample compatibility | Full API documentation is published with DocC: [https://bbc6bae9.github.io/a2ui-swift/documentation/](https://bbc6bae9.github.io/a2ui-swift/documentation/) ## Built-In Components | Category | Components | | --- | --- | | Content | Text, Image, Icon, AudioPlayer, Video | | Layout | Row, Column, List, Card, Tabs, Divider, Modal | | Input | Button, TextField, CheckBox, Slider, DateTimeInput, ChoicePicker | Agents can only use components that your client exposes through a catalog. This keeps the runtime boundary explicit: the model can request UI, but your app decides what is allowed. ## Data Binding And Actions A2UI-Swift supports the core interaction model needed for real agent workflows: - surfaces can be created, updated, and deleted through A2UI messages; - components can read from and write to the surface data model; - expressions can format, validate, and derive values; - checks can disable invalid actions before they are sent; - templates can render repeated UI from arrays or dictionaries; - user actions are resolved into structured client actions for your transport layer. That means an agent can stream a form, update a list, validate input, and receive structured user intent without executing code inside your app. ## Custom Components Most production apps already have their own design system. A2UI-Swift is designed for that. Register custom components in a catalog, map A2UI properties to your native view, and keep all rendering logic inside your app: ```swift let catalog = CustomComponentCatalog( catalogId: "com.example.travel", components: [ HotelCardComponent(), FlightOptionComponent(), ApprovalSummaryComponent(), ] ) ``` Custom catalogs let agents compose with your trusted building blocks instead of inventing UI code. ## Sample Apps ### `travel_app` An end-to-end generative AI sample that combines A2UI-Swift with custom components and real agent interactions. The A2A protocol client lives in [a2a-swift](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2a-swift) and is consumed as a remote SwiftPM dependency.

### Component spec (maps 1:1 to the A2UI catalog names)

Core components:

- **Orb**
  - Props: `state` (idle | listening | thinking | speaking | done), `size` (32 | 104).
  - States: idle breathes (4000ms); listening shows rings (1200ms loop); thinking uses a conic gradient with an orbiting arc (1100ms); speaking ripples (1600ms); done draws a check, then returns to idle after 4s.
  - Size: 32 inside a 44 halo in the Pill; 104 as the hero.
- **Pill**
  - Props: `state`, `label`, `onHide`, `onStop`.
  - States: idle is compact (orb plus "Look and say", no Hide/Stop); listening, thinking, speaking and done have the same layout and a different label; the awaiting-confirm label is `Listening for "yes"`.
  - Size: height 58, padding 6, gap 6, radius full; Hide and Stop are 40 on desktop, 44 on iPhone.
- **Panel**
  - Props: `context`, `cards`, `checkpoint`, `chips`, `input`, `mode` (default | large).
  - Slot order: ContextRow, then card, then ConfirmCard, then IntentChips, then InputRow.
  - Size: width 560 (480-600), padding 18, gap 14, radius 24; large mode is 800 wide.
  - On iPhone it is a full-width bottom sheet (glass-sheet, radius 24 on top, padding 16).
  - It sits 8 below the Pill, next to the gaze target, never as a sidebar.
- **IntentChip**
  - Props: `icon`, `label`, `state` (default | hover | active | disabled), `onSelect`.
  - Size: desktop 13/16, padding 4/8, radius 10, dot separators, at most 4.
  - On iPhone: 36-tall capsules in a horizontal scroll row.
  - Hidden in large mode, where two big buttons replace them.
- **InputRow**
  - Props: `state` (idle | listening | typing | disabled), `value`, `placeholder`, `shortcut`, `onSubmit`, `onMic`.
  - States: idle shows the placeholder and the shortcut hint; listening shows the live transcript with a caret; typing turns the mic into a send button.
  - Size: height 52, radius 16, round action button 36.

A2UI card catalog:

- **ConflictCard**
  - Props: `event {title, start, end, calendar, guests}`, `conflictsWith`, `options [move {to}, skip, keep]`, `selected` (null | move | skip | keep), `onSelect`.
  - States: unresolved; move, skip or keep selected, shown with an accent-soft fill and a check.
  - Move and Skip open a ConfirmCard; Keep changes nothing.
  - Size: option buttons 40 tall on desktop, 44 on iPhone.
- **TrainCard**
  - Props: `line`, `dep {time, station, platform}`, `arr {time, station}`, `duration`, `transfers`, `walk {minutes, arrive}`, `openUrl`.
  - States: default and selected.
  - The SBB tile is 36 in service red, the times use text-time, and the meta uses text-meta.
  - On iPhone the timeline collapses to "17:31 → 17:57" with the line badge.
- **EventCard**
  - Props: `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`, `source` (domain of the page being looked at), `status` (new | in-calendar).
  - States: new shows an accent badge; in-calendar shows a success badge.
  - Date tile 52x56.
- **ReminderCard**
  - Props: `time`, `offset`, `anchor`, `previewText`, `onChange`, `onUndo`.
  - States: set and changed.

# Ensure a project worktree follows the agent-memory file convention.
# AGENTS.md is the real project-intrinsic knowledge file; CLAUDE.md is a
# real regular file whose canonical content is the two-line @AGENTS.md pointer
# that Claude Code inlines at load time. Creates a minimal AGENTS.md skeleton

# CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md symlink into the pointer file, and refuses to clobber
# distinct real files or wrong symlinks.
# Owns the canonical "## Maintaining this file" self-governance wording for
# project AGENTS.md files, injecting it idempotently into created skeletons,
# promoted CLAUDE.md files, and existing AGENTS.md files lacking both the exact
# heading and the project-owned mark below (exact first line, LF or CRLF):
# <!-- firstmate:maintained-by-project -->
# Projects may place this mark at the start of the file and retain equivalent
# maintenance guidance under their own heading. It declares guidance is present, not
# permission to remove governance. No prose equivalence is inferred.
# Owns the canonical CLAUDE.md pointer content (the exact two-line @AGENTS.md
# form). A real-file pointer cannot follow a write into AGENTS.md, which is why
# the installer never creates a CLAUDE.md symlink.
# Refuses a case-variant real memory file such as a lowercase agents.md, so the
# pointer's @AGENTS.md import resolves to a real AGENTS.md on a case-sensitive

# uppercase-literal-target dangling-symlink hazard that a CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md
# link would have carried for that same mismatch.
# This is a worktree utility for crewmates, not a supervision script, so it does

# Frontend: BeaverAgent (iPhone app)

WP1 from [docs/work-packages.md](../docs/work-packages.md).
The WebSocket, Cards and A2UI sections of [docs/contracts.md](../docs/contracts.md) are the API.

## Build and run

Open `BeaverAgent/BeaverAgent.xcodeproj` in Xcode and run the `BeaverAgent` scheme, or build from the command line:

```sh
xcodebuild -project frontend/BeaverAgent/BeaverAgent.xcodeproj -scheme BeaverAgent \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -derivedDataPath ./.derived build
```

For the demo iPhone, pick your own team under Signing & Capabilities.

`a2ui-swift` is pinned to upstream revision `16476ba`, not `from: "0.3.0"`.
Every 0.3.x tag depends on `swift-foundation-icu` by revision, which SwiftPM refuses under a version requirement, and that commit drops the dependency.
Move back to a version rule once a tag after 0.3.5 is released.

## Modes

The app starts in fixture mode ("Demo data"): typed questions replay the bundled fixtures as server frames, through the same decoding and rendering path as live frames.
Questions about flights, events or the week return the event and flight cards; anything else returns the demo reply.
Turn off "Use demo data" in settings and enter the tunnel URL and `APP_TOKEN` to go live.

Touch and hold the orb to type a question (the `text` frame).
In fixture mode the same sheet can pretend a screenshot arrived, which shows the screen chip.

## Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `Protocol.swift` | Wire types for `/ws` |
| `WebSocketClient.swift` | `hello`, frame decoding, reconnect after 1 s and on foreground |
| `AgentSession.swift` | Screen state for the latest turn, fixture replay |
| `CardsView.swift` | A2UI surfaces; `nativeCards` is the switch point for native fallback cards |
| `OrbView.swift` | Orb states and the status pill |
| `Theme.swift` | Design tokens from the Paper design system, light and dark |
| `Fixtures/` | `demo_reply.json`, `cards.json`, `screen.json` from WP2; `demo_a2ui.json`, `cards_a2ui.json` stand in for WP3's files |

When WP3 pushes `backend/fixtures/demo_a2ui.json` and `cards_a2ui.json`, copy them over the files in `Fixtures/`.

## Screenshots and rehearsals

Launch arguments set up a state without tapping through it:

```sh
xcrun simctl launch <udid> ch.microintent.BeaverAgent -appearance dark -demoScene searching
```

| Argument | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `-demoScene` | `listening`, `thinking`, `searching`, `speaking`, `reply`, `kinds`, `screen`, `error` |
| `-demoSheet` | `settings`, `debug` |
| `-demoAsk` | A question sent 2 s after launch, live or in fixture mode |
| `-appearance` | `system`, `light`, `dark` |
| `-largeText` | `YES`, `NO` |
| `-useFixtures`, `-serverURL`, `-token` | Override the settings for one launch |

The WP1 iPhone UI is done (tasks 1-5 and 8) and the PR is out of draft, waiting for review: https://github.com/Orb-agent/micro-intent/pull/5. It targets `develop` from `feature/wp1-ios-ui`; nothing is merged.

The checks were a successful simulator build and a visual pass over every state in the simulator, in dark and light. All 24 screenshots are embedded in the PR and copied to `data/micro-intent-ios-ui-v1/screenshots/`. There are no test suites, per the brief.

**What's built:**
- **Xcode project** at `frontend/BeaverAgent`: SwiftUI, iOS 17, microphone permission text, and a2ui-swift as the only package.
- **Fixtures** from Igor's branch, plus my own A2UI fixtures that stand in for WP3's two files until they land.
- **Cards** render through A2UI, styled as dark glass. All four card types show in light and dark. There's a clear switch point for the other worker's native fallback cards; I didn't build those.
- **Orb** with idle, listening, thinking, searching and speaking, a status label under it, and a speech bubble showing `reply.say`.
- **Settings** for server URL and token, plus demo-data, large-text and appearance options. The WebSocket client follows the contract. Touch-and-hold on the orb opens a typed-question sheet.
- **Screen chip** on `screen_ok`. It fades after 2 minutes and says when the screen couldn't be read.
- **Design**: values come from the Paper Variant D file and the design tokens you sent. From the team's research notes I took the "What do you need?" idle screen, a one-line "Checked trains" trail, and follow-up question chips.

**Live test:** I ran Igor's stub server locally, unchanged, and the app behaved correctly against it:
- A typed question goes through thinking and "Checking trains…" to the reply.
- A wrong token shows "The server rejected the token."
- The app reconnects on its own after the server restarts.
- A screenshot upload without a vision key shows the "couldn't read" chip.

Igor's branch has no `a2ui.py` yet, so live replies show no cards until WP3's code lands.

**Things the team should know:**
- **a2ui-swift version:** `from: "0.3.0"` doesn't resolve. Every 0.3.x release pulls in a dependency pinned in a way SwiftPM rejects. I pinned the project to upstream commit `16476ba` (after 0.3.5), which removes that dependency. `docs/contracts.md` still says `from: "0.3.0"`; I left the contract unchanged and explained it in the PR.

- **Entire** was active throughout, and its checkpoint refs are on origin.
- **Disk** is down to about 8.8 GB free, close to the 8 GB stop line. My build cache (`./.derived`, about 0.8 GB) is still there.

My app is stopped, the stub server is shut down, and the iPhone 17 Pro simulator is still booted.
